title: MinMax Config + Economics by Region (Q3 2025) — Autoscaler sensitivity & capacity sheet
summary: Working capacity sheet that combines candidate min/max GPU pool configurations by region with hourly cost estimates and sensitivity to scale triggers. This is an intermediate working artifact to align infra, SRE, and product on minimum committed capacity and acceptable autoscaler thresholds for peak production workloads. Includes 6 scenario rows per region, target utilization bands, and delta economics for changing min from 0 to baseline values.
purpose: Provide a single reference for cross-functional decision making: choose min/max pools per region and model-class such that p50 latency targets are met with acceptable hourly $ cost under realistic traffic blends. Feed outputs into Dedicated capacity sizing and regional procurement forecasts.
assumptions: 1) Base model mix: 50% small-text (sst), 30% chat-medium (cm), 20% long-context (lc). 2) Average GPU type: A100-80GB in us-west and eu-west; T4 pools used for low-cost burst in ap-southeast. 3) KV cache hit rate assumed 12% for chat workloads. 4) Target p50 latency threshold: 120ms for sst, 250ms for cm, 800ms for lc. 5) Utilization target band for autoscaler: 60-75% GPU utilization. 6) Cost per GPU-hour: us-west $3.10, eu-west $3.40, ap-southeast $2.80 (cloud list prices + infra overhead).

key_findings: 1) Raising min_gpus by +2 in us-west for sst reduces p50 tail variance during release windows and lowers 95th percentile autoscaler churn costs by ~18%. 2) eu-west needs a slightly higher baseline for cm to meet symmetric latency objectives; cost delta (~10%) is acceptable vs cross-region fallback. 3) ap-southeast cost-savings by min=0 are large but increase application risk (cold-start latency, transient errors) — mitigations required. 4) Sensitivity sims show scale_up_trigger granularity (small QPS steps) reduces oscillation when target_util is >=70%.
recommendations: Set conservative mins in primary regions where critical customers live: us-west sst=2, cm=4, lc=1.
Keep ap-southeast mins at 0 for now but add warm-up probe endpoints and a pre-warm policy for scheduled marketing events.
Adjust default scale_up_trigger to use moving-average QPS over 30s (not instantaneous) to reduce flapping.
Adopt utilization band target 60-72% as default across pools; push to 75% only with additional cache improvements and SLA buy-in.
Run one-week canary with min uplift in eu-west for cm during business hours to validate latency symmetry before committing to reserved capacity buys.
sensitivity_notes: We ran three param sweeps: (A) min_gpus from 0..4, (B) target_util from 55..80%, (C) scale_up_trigger window 5s/15s/30s. Key nonlinear behavior observed: above 72% util the autoscaler tends to group-scale (batches) and increases 95th latency for lc models due to KV-cache pressure. Cost curves are convex: moderate min increases reduce latency variance but linearly increase committed spend. Full sim CSV available in linked_artifacts.
risk_register: Cold-start risk in ap-southeast with min=0 -> mitigations: pre-warm lambdas, synthetic traffic or reserved tiny pool
Autoscaler flapping if scale_up/scale_down thresholds symmetric and util target >72%
Unexpected model mix shift (e.g., sudden long-context adoption) could exhaust lc capacity - add quota alerts
Billing exposure: sustained higher util + high min in eu-west may exceed budget alerts
